summary: Cache-side memory throughput and load-dependency stalls limit the kernel, rather than DRAM bandwidth or compute.
reasoning: Memory SOL is 71.35% versus 38.7% compute throughput. L2 throughput reaches 75.21%, while DRAM throughput is only 16.32% with a 95.62% L2 hit rate, locating the pressure primarily in the cache-side memory path. Long-scoreboard stalls reach 61.98%.

root_causes.cause: Low global-load sector utilization increases cache traffic for operand loads.

evidence.interpretation: Global loads use only half of each sector on average, increasing traffic relative to useful bytes.
Elevated L2 throughput makes inefficient operand accesses costly even when DRAM traffic is low.

fixes.fix: Profile A/B load instructions and specialize operand layouts for the actual strides, packing a poorly coalesced operand into a contiguous layout when needed.
fixes.rationale: Improved coalescing can increase useful bytes per sector and reduce L2 traffic; include packing cost when benchmarking.

root_causes.cause: Outstanding operand-load dependencies are insufficiently hidden by active warps and pipeline overlap.

evidence.interpretation: Warps frequently wait for dependencies associated with L1TEX operations, consistent with exposed operand-load latency.
Moderate achieved occupancy limits the pool of warps available to hide latency.
Shared memory imposes a tighter block-residency limit than registers, whose limit is nine blocks.

fixes.fix: Extend autotuning to compare num_stages=2 against the existing 3–4 stages for the same tile sizes, selecting by runtime and long-scoreboard stalls.
fixes.rationale: Fewer stages may reduce shared-memory usage and improve residency; measurement is necessary because reduced prefetch overlap can offset that benefit.
